samples.summary: Durability is decided from a second, uncached `me` query, so every durable document is first attached on the ambient client and then unmounted and re-attached on the durable one
samples.evidence: `useQuery({queryKey:['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional})` (line 165-169) is a *different* query key from the `['me']` query `PrivateRoute.tsx:13` already resolved, so on a private route `me` is `undefined` for the first renders. With `userId` undefined, `useDurableDocument` computes `eligible=false` → `settled = !eligible = true` (use-durable-document.ts:203), so line 199's guard passes and line 203-205 renders `inner` — the ambient `DocumentProvider` mounts and attaches the document. When the optional query resolves, `eligible` flips true, `subject` changes, `answered` becomes false, `settled` becomes false, and line 199-201 returns `null`: the whole editor subtree (DocumentProvider + editor + its local state) unmounts and detaches, then re-mounts under `DurableYorkieProvider`. This is precisely the sequence the comment at lines 188-198 says must not happen ("an edit made in that window would live in a client React is about to unmount, which offline is exactly where it would be lost"). It fires on every durable document open on a fresh page load, and the same path is retravelled whenever the `me` query refetches to a different/absent value.

samples.summary: `durable` is never falsified by store write failures, so the chip promises "Saved to this device" (and disarms the unload/navigation guards) while nothing is being persisted
samples.evidence: `sync-state.ts:41-47` documents `durable` as "the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, **and the store is not failing its writes**". The third conjunct is not implemented: `setLost`/`reportLoss` is called only from `DurableLossWatch`'s `local-changes-dropped` subscription (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:160-163) — grep shows no other caller. A `QuotaExceededError` that survives `withQuotaRetry` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1010-1013), an `InvalidStateError` from `refuseIfEvicted` (line 617-626, which can also never fire for an eviction performed by *another* tab's store instance since `evicted` is per-instance), or a failed attach that leaves `useYorkie().error` set with any code other than `ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere` all leave `durable === true`. `sync-status-chip.tsx:106-109` then computes `stranded=false` and `mayHaveUnsent=false`, so neither the `beforeunload` handler nor `useNavigationGuard` is registered, and the user is told the work is on disk when it is not. Closing the tab loses it silently.

samples.summary: The durable provider's `WafflebaseDocStore` is never closed, leaking an IndexedDB connection per mounted document
samples.evidence: The store is built in `useMemo(..., [userId])` with no `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()`. `WafflebaseDocStore.close()` exists precisely so "a `deleteDatabase` elsewhere is not blocked" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:403-408) and every other construction site (`offline-erase.ts:77`, `offline-erase.ts:107`, `offline-runtime.tsx:90`) closes. Navigating between documents in a session accumulates open `IDBDatabase` handles that are only reclaimed by GC/page unload.

samples.summary: `collectStale` sweeps entries and archives across *all* users, unlike every other cleanup path which is user-scoped
samples.evidence: `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` (line 873) and `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 886) query only by timestamp, with no `userId` filter — contrast `evictOldest` (line 1034-1036), `dropAllForUser` (line 843) and `listArchives` (line 787), all of which scope to `this.userId` precisely because "the database is per origin". On a shared device, signing in as A and letting `OfflineRuntime` run its once-per-session sweep deletes B's aged entries *and* B's archives — and an archive is the only copy of work the SDK could not reconcile.

samples.summary: Replay contiguity is only checked between consecutive log entries, not against the snapshot, so a log missing its head is replayed and reported as `complete: true`
samples.evidence: `let expected: number | undefined;` starts undefined and is only set after the first entry is accepted (lines 148, 164). A log whose first stored `clientSeq` is not snapshot+1 — the shape a torn append or a partial eviction leaves, which is exactly the population this recovery path serves — passes the loop with `truncatedAt === undefined`, so line 194 reports `complete: true` for a document that is silently missing its earliest unsent edits. The comment at lines 140-145 says truncation exists precisely so "a plausible-looking one missing an edit, handed back with no sign that anything is absent" cannot be produced.

samples.summary: `standDown` performs the `release()` side effect inside a `setState` updater, which React may invoke more than once or discard
samples.evidence: `setDecision((current) => { ...; current.session.release(); return { subject: current.subject }; })` — state updaters must be pure. Under StrictMode double-invocation or a concurrent render that is thrown away, the Web Lock is released while the returned state can be discarded, leaving `durable === true` and `clientKey` reported for a document whose election this tab no longer holds — the two-tabs-one-stable-actor case the whole module exists to prevent. The release should be done in the callback body (or an effect) with the state update following it.

samples.summary: A transient 401 (session expiry) routes through `logout()` and erases all locally persisted unsent work
samples.evidence: `fetchWithAuth` (line 228-235) calls `logout({redirect:false, suppressFailure:true})` on any 401 whose refresh failed, and `logout()` now unconditionally `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (line 105), which runs `dropAllForUser` — deleting the live entries *and* the archives of work that could not be reconciled. A session that merely expired (cookie lapse, refresh endpoint hiccup) therefore destroys offline edits the user could still have pushed after signing back in, with no prompt. The design's intent is erase on explicit sign-out; this path is not distinguished.

On first render me is undefined, so userId is undefined, eligible is false (use-durable-document.ts:115-120) and settled is true (use-durable-document.ts:203) — line 199's guard passes and lines 203-205 mount the ambient DocumentProvider, attaching the document. The existing regression test mocks useQuery to return identity synchronously (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:70-73, 210-223), so it cannot see this window. The only thing suppressing it today is the build-time pin @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 < MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67; package.json:65), which that file explicitly describes as the single switch that turns the feature on — a version pin, not a guard, so it does not make the defect unreal or unreachable by design.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `durable` originates only at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:104-109 and is lowered only by `reportLoss`, whose single production caller is the `local-changes-dropped` subscription at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:160-163 (repo-wide grep for reportLoss/setLost/expectLoss across all packages, docs and scripts returns no other caller). Store write failures are unobservable to the provider: withQuotaRetry rethrows QuotaExceededError (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1000-1016) and refuseIfEvicted throws InvalidStateError (617-626), and WafflebaseDocStoreOptions (104-138) exposes no failure callback; the only other durability-lowering path, LockRefusalWatch (186-200), matches only ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere. The value flows via durable-document-context.ts:67-69 -> use-sync-status.ts:75,220 -> sync-state.ts:85 -> sync-status-chip.tsx:106-109, where `saved-locally` makes stranded=false and mayHaveUnsent=false, so neither the beforeunload listener (119-130) nor useNavigationGuard (142) is registered while the chip reads "Saved to this device" (LABELS line 41). The repo's own task note (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:132-134) concedes write failures do not lower it, while sync-state.ts:43-45 still documents that conjunct as part of the contract — so the promise is made and not kept. Real correctness/data-loss defect on a reachable failure path (quota exhaustion, evicted base, IDB write errors); no counterexample exists.

finding.summary: Replay contiguity is only checked between consecutive log entries, not against the snapshot, so a log missing its head is replayed and reported as `complete: true`
finding.evidence: `let expected: number | undefined;` starts undefined and is only set after the first entry is accepted (lines 148, 164). A log whose first stored `clientSeq` is not snapshot+1 — the shape a torn append or a partial eviction leaves, which is exactly the population this recovery path serves — passes the loop with `truncatedAt === undefined`, so line 194 reports `complete: true` for a document that is silently missing its earliest unsent edits. The comment at lines 140-145 says truncation exists precisely so "a plausible-looking one missing an edit, handed back with no sign that anything is absent" cannot be produced.

verdict.reason: The code matches the finding exactly. In rehydrateArchive, `expected` is declared undefined (offline-copy.ts:148) and the contiguity test `expected !== undefined && change.clientSeq !== expected` (offline-copy.ts:152) therefore never applies to the first log entry; `expected` is first assigned only after that entry is accepted (offline-copy.ts:164). No code compares the first stored clientSeq against the snapshot's position, even though the snapshot document is available (offline-copy.ts:132) and `getCheckpoint().getClientSeq()` is used elsewhere in this codebase (use-sync-status.ts:111). Consequently a log missing its head leaves `truncatedAt === undefined` and line 194 reports `complete: true`, contradicting the module's own stated invariant (offline-copy.ts:93-97, 140-145). No upstream guard establishes head contiguity: the store archives whatever change rows exist (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:697-709) and only saveSnapshot trims the log (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:489-509). The sole consumer trusts `complete` verbatim and, on the reported-complete path, calls `dropArchive`, destroying the last copy (offline-copy-recovery.ts:159-185). I could not verify that the SDK's restoreAppendedChanges throws on a non-contiguous head (the dependency is not present in the tree), so the catch at offline-copy.ts:171 cannot be cited as an existing guard; existing tests only cover mid-log gaps (offline-copy.test.ts:195-214), never a missing head. Real, reachable on the recovery path, and in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Durable documents attach on the ambient client first, then the whole editor is unmounted and re-attached, because `me` is undefined on the first render
finding.evidence: `useDurableDocument({ userId: me?.id === undefined ? undefined : String(me.id) })` (line 171-174). On the first render of any owned editor, `me` is `undefined` because the query key here is `['me','optional']` while every owned editor route primes `['me']` (document-detail.tsx:852, docs-detail.tsx:331, notes-detail.tsx:358, slides-detail.tsx:940, board-detail.tsx:241; only PublicRoute/shared-document/sheet-view use `['me','optional']`). With `me` undefined, `eligible` is false, `settled` is `!eligible` = true, so `inner` renders and the document attaches on the ambient client. When the query resolves, `eligible` flips true, `subject` changes, `answered` is false, so `settled` becomes false and line 199-201 `return null` unmounts the entire `DocumentProvider` subtree (detach + editor state destroyed), then re-mounts it under `DurableYorkieProvider`. That is precisely the 'attach the document twice on every durable open — and an edit made in that window would live in a client React is about to unmount' failure the comment at lines 188-198 claims is prevented. The new durable test suite mocks `useQuery` to return `me` synchronously, so it cannot see this.

verdict.reason: The code matches the finding exactly. `CollabDocumentProvider` reads identity under `['me','optional']` (collab-document-provider.tsx:165-169), while every owned editor route primes only `['me']` (notes-detail.tsx:358, docs-detail.tsx:331, document-detail.tsx:852, slides-detail.tsx:940, board-detail.tsx:241) — and no setQueryData/initialData seeds `['me','optional']` anywhere, so `me` is undefined on the first render of an owned editor. With `userId` undefined, `eligible` is false (use-durable-document.ts:115-120) and `settled` is `!eligible` = true (line 203), so `inner` renders and the document attaches on the ambient client. When the query resolves and the feature is eligible, `subject` (line 135) changes, `answered` (line 181) is false, `settled` goes false, and collab-document-provider.tsx:199-201 returns null — unmounting the entire DocumentProvider subtree (detach + editor state destroyed) before remounting under DurableYorkieProvider. That is precisely the attach-twice/edit-in-a-doomed-client failure the comment at lines 188-198 claims is prevented, and the durable test suite cannot see it because it mocks useQuery to return `me` synchronously (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:70-73). The only thing making this dormant today is the version gate supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:61-67) against the 0.7.22 pin (packages/frontend/package.json:65); that is an enablement flag the repo says is flipped by a one-line dependency bump, not a guard on this path, so it does not support refutation.

finding.summary: A 401 session expiry erases the offline archives, destroying the only copy of work the SDK could not reconcile
finding.evidence: `logout()` now awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (auth.ts:105), which calls `store.dropAllForUser(who)`; `dropAllForUser` deletes live entries *and* `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:851). `logout()` is not only user-initiated: `fetchWithAuth` calls it on any 401 whose refresh failed (auth.ts:229). An archive is, by this feature's own design, the sole remaining copy of unsent edits the SDK gave up reconciling and which the recovery UI is supposed to hand back. So an expired session — a routine event, reachable from any background request — silently and irreversibly deletes that work before the user is ever offered it. The erase-on-sign-out intent does not cover an involuntary token expiry.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out in the repository. `logout()` unconditionally awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (auth.ts:105), which resolves the remembered user and calls `store.dropAllForUser(who)` (offline-erase.ts:65-79, :30); `dropAllForUser` deletes live entries and then `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, IDBKeyRange.only(userId))` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:842-853, deletion at :851). `logout()` is reached involuntarily from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm after a failed refresh (auth.ts:221-236, call at :229), which any background authenticated request can hit on routine session expiry. The archive is by design the only remaining copy of edits the SDK could not reconcile: `offerRecoverableWork` lists them and offers them back (offline-runtime.tsx:106-176), and `recoverOfflineCopy` deliberately drops the archive only after the copy is written (offline-copy-recovery.ts:152-185). I looked for a guard making this unreachable and found only `if (!who) return` (offline-erase.ts:68); `signedInUserId` is set for the whole authenticated session by `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` in `OfflineRuntime` (offline-runtime.tsx:42) and cleared only on unmount (:89), so during a live session the erase does fire. The design's stated trigger is "Logout | Drop every entry for that user" (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:214) with rationale about deliberate sign-out on a shared device; it does not contemplate involuntary token expiry. Irreversible loss of the user's only copy of unsent work on a routine path is data loss, squarely in the correctness lane and critical by the rubric.
